2. Opposite party no. 1 on or about 21.07.03 made an application under section 24 of the Non-Agriculture Tenancy Act, 1949, hereinafter referred to as the Act in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge at Nesarabad in Pirojpur being Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 2003 against the vendee and others for preemption of the case land measuring about 1.0625 of plot no. 360 appertaining to SA Khatian no. 282 transferred by a  deed of sale being no. 1448/2003 dated 08.06.03 by opposite party no. 2 to the vendee. 

 3. Case of the preemptor was that one Snehalata was owner-in-possession of 53 decimals of land that is one fourth of said plot no. 360 appertaining to said SA khatian no. 282. After her death, her son Nripen Chandra Ich Sarker by several deeds dated 09.05.83 transferred 20 decimals of said plot along with other land to Moulana Nur Mohammad Khandakar. Then, by a registered deed dated 16.2.91 said Nur Mohammad transferred by way of gift said 20 decimals of land to his daughter Mursheda Khanam Nashrin, the preemptor and delivered possession. Since then she lived in said 20 decimals of land. So, she became a co-tenant in said land of plot no. 360. 

 5. The vendee opposed the application by filing a written objection denying the case of the preemptor. He contended that the case was bad for defect of parties and also barred by limitation. He further contended that Snehalata was owner in possession of 53 decimals of land that is one fourth of plot no. 360 appertaining to SA Khatian no. 282. After her death, her son Nripen Chandra Ich Sarker became owner in possession of said 53 decimals of land of case plot. Rest 1.57 acres of land of plot no. 360 was recorded in SA Khatian no. 46. Being owner in possession of said SA Khatian no. 46, Nripendra on 18.05.93 by a registered deed being no. 1115 transferred 7 decimals of land to the vendee. By building house thereon, the vendee was living in said land. After death of Nripen Chandra Ich Sarker, his three sons namely Ramprashad Sarker minor, Devaprashad Sarker and Shyam Prashad Ich Sarker minor became owners in possession. On 14.02.96 they made an agreement for transfer of 3.75 acres of land to the vendee. When the vendee demanded a right of passage for egress from his house, Ranjita Rani Ich agreed to transfer said 1.0625 and then Ranjita Rani Ich transferred 3.125 decimals of land of plot no. 360 appertaining to SA Khanna no. 46 by a registered deed dated 27.02.96 pursuant to an agreement dated 14.02.96 and delivered possession. Said Ranjita Rani Ich transferred 1.0625 decimals of land by impugned kabala dated 08.06.03. The vendee since possessed the passage. 

 12. I find opposite party no.2 transferred the case land measuring 1.0625 decimals of plot no. 360 appertaining to SA Khatian No. 282 to the vendee by a deed of sale dated 08.06.03, exhibit—Gha. It also appears from the record that the preemptor became a co-tenant in the case land of said SA plot 360 by way of a gift from her father as back as on 16.02.91. The vendee also claimed to be a co-tenant in said plot no.360 by purchase with registered deeds of sale dated 18.5.93 and 27.2.96 exhibit—Ka and Kha. But both the deeds relate to SA Khatian No 46 not to SA Khatian No. 282. SA Khatian No. 282 covers 53 decimals of land of plot No. 360 and was recorded in the name of Snehalala only, exhibit-1 and SA Kantian No. 46 covers 1.57 acres of plot no. 360 and was recorded in the names of Upendra Nath and others. It is not unnatural for the same land of a CS plot to be splitted into two different holdings in the survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. After splitting of said CS plot, land of one SA khatian cannot be said to be the same land of other SA khatian. A tenant in land of SA plot no. 360 of SA khatian no. 46 is not a co-tenant of the land of same SA plot no. 360 of SA khatian no. 282. 

 13. In view of the decision in SM Nasirul Hoq v Omar Farooq Chowdhury (2002), 54 DLR 181 authored by me, the vendee by purchase of land of plot no. 360 of Khatian No. 46 did not become a co-tenant in the land of plot No. 360 appertaining to SA Khatian No. 282, he was a stranger under the Act.
